root_cause: At s7468 r1 P1 (the one finding V9 still reproduces as a home capture) Gamma's 'Move obj_home_1' scored 38.1 vs 24.4 for Advance obj_nml_1 and 14.7 for Advance obj_center. The gap comes from objective-level heuristics, not VP: objective_priority 26.7 for home vs 23.2 for NML, because WEIGHT_HOME_UNDEFENDED (+9) is added to any home objective with friendly_oc 0. On top of that home got reachability +3 (one-turn trip, no distance penalty) and secondary_defend_home +2.45, while the centre carried contest_race -13.1. The card (Smoke and Mirrors) pays nothing for home: hold_min excludes home, and MissionManager never decoys a home objective. expected_vp=2 for home is a mis-estimate: the decoyed_* rule is treated as 'counts'. No Ork unit could reach home before P1's next turn. After Gamma took home, the replan sent Alpha there as a 'reinforcing' second unit (the home bonus stays on until the objective is actually held). A vs B (base, 2 seeds): B gained in round 1 at end of turn, decoyed_score +6 vs +2 (Gamma forward lets a forward objective be decoyed); round-2 primary was equal. 2-seed effect was -5.0 [-8.9,-1.1] (noise vs the 36-seed +6.86). The other three findings are not this cause on V9: s7451 P2 is a Normal-vs-Advance mode choice on a centre trip (the [ASSAULT] question, untouched by this design). In s7412 and s7411 V9 already Advances to obj_center at the decision point and does not go home (drift: not reproduced).
fix_summary: FIX_R1_HOME_CAPTURE (const 1.0, get_param). In _assign_units_to_objectives pass 2 and the COORD-4 backfill, a move/advance candidate to our own home objective is skipped when all of these hold: battle round 1, home is 'uncontrolled', the unit is not already on it, the primary card pays nothing for holding it (KEEPER-RELEASE's _keeper_release_primary_counts with a new optional flag that skips decoyed_* rules for home, since a home objective cannot be decoyed), and no enemy can be in range by the end of the enemy's next turn (KEEPER-RELEASE's _keeper_release_threat). The unit then falls through to its next candidate. Keepers (units on home) and every later round are untouched. Logs '[R1_HOME_CAPTURE] <obj>: not sending <unit> ...'. Value 0 restores the base exactly: the closure returns false, and the new flag defaults to false for KEEPER-RELEASE.

fires: Counted from game stdout over 9 replays (4 findings + 5 guardrails, both players, played to the end of round 2). It fired only in s7468 P1 round 1: 3 lines (Gamma C, then Beta B and Alpha A in the next replans, all for obj_home_1). 0 lines in the other 8 games. Round 1 only, so at most one player turn per game per side, and only when home is empty, unpaid and unreachable by the enemy.
risks: (1) Home stays empty through round 1. When the enemy threat appears later (deep strike / reserves from round 2, fast units), the plan must send someone back. The forward units are then further away, and home could fall in rounds 2-3 to an enemy card that pays for OUR home (hold_enemy_home, e.g. Take and Hold-style rules). (2) The skip applies to EVERY unit, not just a second capturer. At s7468 it also stopped Alpha going home; the forced alternative B kept Alpha going there. Alpha and Beta then stacked on obj_nml_1 (Beta gave up its centre race). Over a full game that can over-commit forward and leave the backfield empty for secondaries such as Defend Stronghold or Area Denial. (3) Primary cards rotate by round: home may pay from round 2 (e.g. a hold_more card), and a round-1 capture would have scored it at the round-2 Command phase. The check only reads the current card. (4) _keeper_release_threat is an over-estimate of reach (Move+12+6, +6 advance-and-charge), so it mostly errs toward keeping the base capture; reserves arriving in round 1 via named abilities are covered, other early-arrival rules may not be. (5) The unit's fallback is whatever candidate is next; with no other objective needing OC it drops to the pass-3 support/screen logic, which may still walk toward home.
